rv.q: This show makes the appeal of the film all the more obvious, even as it also proves how sneakily difficult it is to adapt.
New, exciting musicals are hard to come by, and The Harder They Come features a big cast with big beats — and big potential.
If you love reggae, The Harder They Come is a must.
Still, The Harder They Come is a fun show, as the 25 song inclusions prove (including “The Ballad of Ivan,” a Parks original).
The show will be a revelation to those new to such classic numbers as “You Can Get It If You Really Want”, “Hard Road to Travel”, and the title song, and will delight those who know them well.
Its fidelity to the original is both a boon and a bust.
Stirring musical about youthful resistance to societal oppression
So much top-drawer talent has been poured into this production, it’s dispiriting to see it put in service to such a simplistic scenario.
The stage musical is all about tugging at our heart strings.

Jimmy Cliff’s songs, the indelible spirit of Perry Henzell’s film, Suzan-Lori Parks’ strong book, Tony Taccone’s firm direction, and the impressive work of the creative team all combine to make this new musical a Best Bet for Theatre Reviews Limited.
The cast is uniformly excellent, especially vocally, under the direction of Tony Taccone and Sergio Trujillo...

cn.t: Critics find this reggae-fueled musical adaptation energetic and well-performed, with infectious songs and choreography, but most agree it dilutes the original film's gritty edge and darker themes.
